title: Interest Rates and Stock Prices: An Old Debate Flares up!
gist: US 10-year treasury yields broke out of their post-2022 4-4.5% band to 4.75% by end-August 2026 (20s and 30s above 5%), yet the S&P 500 and NASDAQ rallied because analysts raised 2026 and 2027 S&P 500 earnings estimates by more than 11%. Damodaran argues rates are set by inflation expectations plus real growth — not by new Fed chair Kevin Warsh — and that higher rates hit equities unevenly, with the damage concentrated in CCC credit, consumer, utilities and communications names that lack pricing power.

insights.claim: The US 10-year treasury yield rose from 4.18% at the start of 2026 to 4.75% by August 31, 2026, a breakout from the 4-4.5% range that had held since 2022, while 20-year and 30-year treasuries both crossed 5% during the year.
insights.speaker: Aswath Damodaran
insights.so_what: Long-duration discount rates have reset higher; every DCF, long bond and long-duration equity needs to be re-marked off a ~4.75% base rather than the 4-4.5% assumption that held for four years.
insights.quote: rates since have largely stayed in the 4-4.5% range, with the 4.75% rate in September 2026 representing a breakout
insights.locator: A Longer Term Perspective on Interest Rates

insights.claim: Rates rose more at the long end than the short end during 2026, removing the kink at the 2-year maturity that existed at the start of the year and making the US yield curve more upward sloping.
insights.speaker: Aswath Damodaran
insights.so_what: A steepening driven by the long end favors curve steepener positioning and penalizes long-duration bond portfolios more than bills; it also widens the funding-cost gap for long-dated corporate issuance.
insights.quote: the divergence in rate movement across maturities has removed the kink (at the 2-year maturity) at the start of the year and made the yield curve more upward sloping
insights.locator: The 2026 Interest Rate Experience

insights.claim: The 30-year treasury has historically traded slightly above the 10-year, but that spread widened notably in September 2026.
insights.speaker: Aswath Damodaran
insights.so_what: Widening 10s30s is a term-premium signal worth watching as a tell on whether $40 trillion of US debt is straining long-end demand.
insights.quote: the 30-year treasury rate, which has generally traded at slightly above the 10-year rate, with the difference widening in September 2026
insights.locator: A Longer Term Perspective on Interest Rates

insights.claim: Three linked catalysts pushed rates back to the center of the 2026 market narrative: long-term US treasury rates at twenty-year highs, US debt exceeding $40 trillion for the first time, and uncertainty about the direction new Fed chair Kevin Warsh will take ahead of the mid-September FOMC meeting.
insights.speaker: Aswath Damodaran
insights.so_what: Frames the event risk into mid-September: a Warsh surprise is a positioning risk even if, per Damodaran, it should not move the fundamental rate path.
insights.locator: The war in Iran, oil prices and worries

insights.claim: The four FOMC meetings held in 2026 and Kevin Warsh's ascension to the Fed chairmanship show no visible material impact on treasury rates when plotted against the 2026 rate path.
insights.speaker: Aswath Damodaran
insights.so_what: Fading Fed-meeting-driven rate volatility, rather than trading it, is the implied posture; positioning built around a Warsh pivot has little historical support in the 2026 data.
insights.quote: While there is little in this graph to indicate that the meetings or the changing of the guard at the top had a material impact on treasury rates
insights.locator: The 2026 Interest Rate Experience

insights.claim: Neither Fed chair Kevin Warsh nor Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent can meaningfully alter the trajectory of US rates, because only a break in inflation expectations to the upside or downside will move rates significantly out of their range.
insights.speaker: Aswath Damodaran
insights.so_what: Watch breakeven inflation, not Fed speak, as the signal for the next big rate move; policy-driven rate trades are the wrong trade in this framework.
insights.quote: For rates to change significantly, up or down, there has to be a break in inflation expectations, to the up or downside, and there is little that Kevin Warsh or Scott Bessent can do to alter that trajectory.
insights.locator: Conclusion

insights.claim: The 10-year treasury has been stuck between 4% and 5% since 2022 largely because market-implied expected inflation has settled at about 2.5%, even while actual reported inflation has stayed volatile.
insights.speaker: Aswath Damodaran
insights.so_what: Anchored 2.5% breakevens are the load-bearing assumption for the whole rate range; a breakeven move above ~3% would be the trigger to re-rate long duration sharply lower.
insights.quote: the ten-year US treasury rate has been stuck in a fairly tight range, between 4% and 5%, since 2022, and that is largely because expected inflation has settled in at about 2.5%
insights.locator: Conclusion

insights.claim: An 'intrinsic riskfree rate' computed as the sum of the actual inflation rate and real GDP growth is a usable anchor for where the 10-year treasury should sit, and it tracked the historical rate path across the 1970s inflation surge and the 2009-2021 low-rate era.
insights.speaker: Aswath Damodaran
insights.so_what: Gives investors a simple, replicable fair-value benchmark for the 10-year that does not depend on forecasting the Fed.
insights.quote: an "intrinsic riskfree rate", which I obtain by summing up the inflation rate and real GDP growth in the US economy each year
insights.locator: The Drivers of US Interest Rates

insights.claim: The gap between the intrinsic and actual 10-year rate, which was enormous when inflation surged in 2022, has nearly closed by September 2026, with the actual 10-year at 4.75% against an intrinsic rate of 5.41%.
insights.speaker: Aswath Damodaran
insights.so_what: A residual ~66bp gap implies modest remaining upside to yields on fundamentals — the easy part of the rate normalization is done, but the 10-year is not yet cheap to its anchor.
insights.quote: the intrinsic risk free rate vastly exceeded the actual rate that year, but the difference has narrowed over time, and almost dissipated by September 2026
insights.locator: The Drivers of US Interest Rates

insights.claim: Despite a 2026 surge in oil prices and louder inflation talk, TIPS-implied long-term expected inflation rose only very mildly through the start of September 2026, showing that markets weight long-term expectations far more than year-to-year inflation prints.
insights.speaker: Aswath Damodaran
insights.so_what: The oil spike is not being read as an inflation regime change; inflation-hedge trades premised on oil-driven CPI have little market corroboration.
insights.quote: notwithstanding the surge in oil prices this year, and the increased talk of inflation, there has been only a very mild increase in the long-term expected inflation rate
insights.locator: The Drivers of US Interest Rates

insights.claim: Because the US lost its Moody's Aaa rating in May 2025, the dollar government bond rate is no longer a clean riskfree rate, and a sovereign default spread must be netted out of the treasury yield to derive a true dollar riskfree rate.
insights.speaker: Aswath Damodaran
insights.so_what: Valuation models that plug the raw treasury yield in as the riskfree rate are now overstating the base rate and understating the equity risk premium.
insights.quote: the US lost its Aaa rating (Moody's) in May 2025
insights.locator: Corporate Bonds

themes.theme: Global Rate Convergence and the Death of Carry

insights.claim: Ten-year government bond yields rose across all developed currencies tracked in 2026 — the euro (German bund), Japanese yen, Australian dollar, Canadian dollar and British pound — repeating the pattern of the 2022 surge that lifted the euro rate out of negative territory.
insights.speaker: Aswath Damodaran
insights.so_what: The rate shock is global, so hedging US duration with foreign developed-market duration offers little diversification.
insights.quote: you see the same pattern, with rates rising across all of the currencies tracked in this graph
insights.locator: Government Bond Rates in Other Currencies (Countries)

insights.claim: Emerging-market local rates behaved very differently from developed markets: across the Chinese yuan, Indian rupee, Brazilian real and South African rand there was no or only a muted 2022 effect, and rates were lower in September 2026 than in 2021 in three of the four currencies.
insights.speaker: Aswath Damodaran
insights.so_what: EM local-currency duration has been the structural winner of this cycle and decouples from the DM rate impulse — a non-obvious relative-value case.
insights.quote: rates are lower in September 2026 than they were in 2021 in three of the four currencies
insights.locator: Government Bond Rates in Other Currencies (Countries)

insights.claim: The convergence of government bond rates across currencies in recent years has destroyed the carry trade, and its practitioners deserved the losses because carry's returns came entirely from lags in how exchange rates adjust to fundamentals rather than from any real investment insight.
insights.speaker: Aswath Damodaran
insights.so_what: Strategies and funds whose Sharpe came from rate differentials have lost their engine; do not underwrite carry-dependent return streams as a persistent alpha source.
insights.quote: The carry trade is the laziest of investment strategies, with its successes due entirely to lags in how exchange rates respond to fundamentals, and calling it an investment strategy does a disservice to investing, in general.
insights.locator: Government Bond Rates in Other Currencies (Countries)

themes.theme: Credit: Risk-Free Repricing, Not Spread Stress

insights.claim: Across 2026, corporate default spreads over the 10-year treasury were largely unchanged or lower for every rating class from AAA through B, with the single exception of CCC and below, where the default spread widened by 1.57%.
insights.speaker: Aswath Damodaran
insights.so_what: The stress is idiosyncratic to the lowest tier — a case for staying in IG/BB and underweighting CCC, where the market is starting to price real default risk.
insights.quote: The only ratings class where you see a surge in spreads is in the lowest rated bonds, where the default spread has increased by 1.57% during the course of the year.
insights.locator: Corporate Bonds

insights.claim: Corporate borrowing costs rose globally in 2026 with almost all of the increase coming from rising riskfree rates rather than credit deterioration, meaning cost of capital rose even for borrowers whose credit quality was unchanged.
insights.speaker: Aswath Damodaran
insights.so_what: Hurdle rates are up for everyone; capex and M&A models built on 2024-25 discount rates now understate the required return.
insights.quote: Debt is now costlier than it was at the start of the year, for business borrowers across the world, with almost all of the increase coming from rising riskfree rates
insights.locator: Corporate Bonds

insights.claim: Bond losses in 2026 have been far milder than 2022's because the rate move was smaller and because the price impact of a given rate change is much larger when the starting rate level is very low, as it was in early 2022.
insights.speaker: Aswath Damodaran
insights.so_what: Convexity math means the same basis-point move now does less damage than in 2022 — duration risk is structurally less dangerous from a 4.75% base than from a 1.5% base.
insights.quote: the effect is nowhere near the carnage that we saw in 2022, partly because the rate change has been more muted and partly because the price effect of a rate change is much greater when rates are very low
insights.locator: Corporate Bonds

themes.theme: Why Higher Rates Do Not Mechanically Hurt Stocks

insights.claim: Higher rates hit bonds directly only because the coupon is fixed at issuance, whereas for stocks both the discount rate and the residual cash flows move with rates, so the net valuation effect depends on operating pass-through rather than discounting alone.
insights.speaker: Aswath Damodaran
insights.so_what: The reflexive 'rates up, stocks down' trade is a category error; the right screen is which companies can pass through inflation, not which have long duration.
insights.quote: The reason that the effect of higher rates on value is direct, with bonds, is because the cash flow on a bond is the coupon and the coupon is set at the time the bond is issued, and does not change as interest rates change.
insights.locator: Stock Prices

insights.claim: Whether higher rates damage an equity depends first on why rates rose — inflation versus higher real rates — and if inflation, on how much pricing power the business has to pass that inflation through to customers.
insights.speaker: Aswath Damodaran
insights.so_what: Gives a two-step screen for stock selection in a rising-rate tape: decompose the rate move, then rank holdings by demonstrated pricing power.
insights.locator: With revenues , the key determinants

insights.claim: When rates rise because real rates are rising rather than inflation, companies rationally cut reinvestment as fewer projects clear the hurdle, which raises near-term cash flows at the cost of future growth.
insights.speaker: Aswath Damodaran
insights.so_what: Watch for near-term FCF beats driven by capex cuts rather than operating strength — a quality-of-earnings trap that flatters current multiples while lowering terminal value.
insights.quote: This reduction in reinvestment can increase near-term cashflows, at the expense of future growth.
insights.locator: Stock Prices

insights.claim: Companies split into three groups under higher rates — those whose value falls as the discount-rate effect dominates, those where cash-flow and discount-rate effects cancel, and those whose value rises because cash flows increase more than enough to offset the higher discount rate — so the index-level outcome depends entirely on market composition.
insights.speaker: Aswath Damodaran
insights.so_what: Explains why the same rate move can be bullish for one index and bearish for another; composition, not the rate level, is the variable to analyze.
insights.locator: The effects of higher interest rates will therefore vary

themes.theme: 2026 Equity Resilience and the Earnings Engine

insights.claim: Across 169 trading days from January 1 to August 31, 2026, the 10-year yield rose on 84 days, fell on 73 and was unchanged on 12, and only moves greater than 3 basis points registered in equities — the S&P 500 fell almost half a percent on big-up-yield days and gained about half a percent on big-down-yield days.
insights.speaker: Aswath Damodaran
insights.so_what: There is a tradeable daily rate beta but only above a 3bp threshold — small yield wiggles are noise and should not drive intraday equity positioning.
insights.quote: down almost half a percent on days when the 10-year rate increased by more than 3 basis points and up about half a percent on days when the rate decreased by more than 3 basis points
insights.locator: To zero in on the interest rate effect

insights.claim: Stocks rose strongly over the first eight months of 2026 despite rising yields, yet still systematically underperformed on the specific days when the 10-year rose — an apparent contradiction resolved by earnings revisions swamping the daily rate drag.
insights.speaker: Aswath Damodaran
insights.so_what: Rate sensitivity has not disappeared, it has been outrun by fundamentals — if earnings revisions stall, the latent negative rate beta reasserts itself.
insights.quote: while stocks have held their own during 2026, in the face of rising rates, they have done much worse on days when the 10-year treasury rate went up than they did on days that rate decreased
insights.locator: To zero in on the interest rate effect

insights.claim: Over the first eight months of 2026 sell-side analysts raised S&P 500 earnings estimates by more than 11% for both 2026 and 2027, and this earnings surge — not multiple expansion or rate relief — is the reason equities absorbed higher oil prices, higher rates and political turmoil.
insights.speaker: Aswath Damodaran
insights.so_what: The bull case rests on a single load-bearing variable: forward earnings revisions. Track the revision breadth weekly — a rollover removes the only thing offsetting higher discount rates.
insights.quote: The secret to equity resilience in the face of higher oil prices, interest rates and political turmoil has been in equity earnings, which have surged over the course of 2026.
insights.locator: The secret to equity resilience

insights.claim: Damodaran flags unease about the quality of the 2026 earnings surge, specifically how companies are reporting the effects of AI on their earnings, and promises a dedicated follow-up analysis.
insights.speaker: Aswath Damodaran
insights.so_what: Implied skepticism that AI-related accounting (capitalization, depreciation schedules, cost-savings claims) is inflating reported earnings — the key risk to the pillar holding equities up.
insights.quote: I know that you have questions about these earnings, and I do as well, especially in the context of how companies are reporting the effects of AI on their earnings
insights.locator: Over the first eight months of 2026, analysts

themes.theme: Sector and Regional Dispersion Beneath the Index

insights.claim: Energy was the best performing US sector in 2026 on aggregate market cap, followed by technology, consistent with the year's spike in oil prices.
insights.speaker: Aswath Damodaran
insights.so_what: Confirms energy as the cleanest expression of the 2026 macro mix (oil spike plus pricing power) rather than a defensive rate hedge.
insights.quote: During 2026, energy was the best performing sector , not surprising given the spike in oil prices, followed by technology
insights.locator: Equities: Cross Company Comparisons

insights.claim: Technology's 2026 return is extremely top-heavy: the aggregate tech sector returned 25.22% while the median tech company returned only 7.75%, meaning the largest tech companies produced nearly all the sector's gain.
insights.speaker: Aswath Damodaran
insights.so_what: Equal-weight or small/mid-cap tech exposure has captured almost none of the sector rally — a strong argument against assuming tech-sector beta from a diversified tech book.
insights.quote: the median tech company had returns of only 7.75%, well below the aggregate tech sector returns of 25.22%
insights.locator: Equities: Cross Company Comparisons

insights.claim: The worst performing US sectors through August 2026 were consumer discretionary, consumer staples, utilities and communications, which Damodaran attributes to lower pricing power combined with higher input costs.
insights.speaker: Aswath Damodaran
insights.so_what: Validates the pricing-power framework empirically — short or underweight the margin-squeezed, low-pass-through sectors while rates and input costs stay elevated.
insights.quote: The worst performing sectors in 2026, at least through August, are the consumer sectors (discretionary and staple), utilities and communications, with lower pricing power and higher input costs to blame.
insights.locator: Equities: Cross Company Comparisons

insights.claim: Global equity value rose roughly $17 trillion, or 11.28%, through August 31, 2026, but Indian and Chinese equities lagged badly with low single-digit returns and far more stocks down than up.
insights.speaker: Aswath Damodaran
insights.so_what: Despite falling local rates, Indian and Chinese equities did not participate in the global melt-up — a divergence worth diagnosing before adding EM equity exposure on a rate-relief thesis.
insights.quote: While global equity value has increased about $17 trillion (11.28%) in 2026 (through August 31, 2026), there are wide differences across regions, with Indian and Chinese equities struggling with low single digit returns
insights.locator: Since the rise in interest rates is not restricted

insights.claim: A meaningful portion of cross-regional equity return differences in 2026 is a currency artifact, since dollar-denominated returns are inflated for regions whose currencies appreciated against the dollar and depressed for those that depreciated.
insights.speaker: Aswath Damodaran
insights.so_what: Strip FX before ranking regional equity performance — unhedged dollar-based league tables are measuring currency, not corporate performance.
insights.locator: Some of the performance that you see in this table
